column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|12-11|1911|Ναγκίμπ Μαχφούζ|Naguib Mahfouz|Naguib Mahfouz was an Egyptian writer. He wrote the "Cairo Trilogy" and in 1988 he became the first Arabic-language writer to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2006.

bio|12-11|1918|Αλεξάντρ Σολζενίτσιν|Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn|Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn was a Russian writer. He wrote "One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich" and "The Gulag Archipelago" about the Soviet camps. In 1970 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2008.

bio|12-11|1964|Άλμα Μάλερ|Alma Mahler|Alma Mahler was an Austrian composer and the wife of Gustav Mahler. She later married the architect Walter Gropius and the writer Franz Werfel. She was known for the circle of artists she mixed with. She died in 1964 in New York.
bio|12-12|1821|Γκυστάβ Φλωμπέρ|Gustave Flaubert|Gustave Flaubert was a French writer. He wrote the novel "Madame Bovary", which is regarded as a masterpiece of realism. He died in 1880.

bio|12-12|1843|Γουλιέλμος Α΄|William I of the Netherlands|William I was the first king of the Netherlands, from 1815. He abdicated in 1840 and died in 1843. During his reign the Belgian Revolution of 1830 brought independence to Belgium.
bio|12-12|1863|Έντβαρτ Μουνκ|Edvard Munch|Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter of Expressionism. He painted the famous work "The Scream", which expresses anguish. He died in 1944.

bio|12-12|1915|Φρανκ Σινάτρα|Frank Sinatra|Frank Sinatra was an American singer and actor. He recorded hits such as "My Way" and "New York, New York" and won an Oscar for the film "From Here to Eternity". He died in 1998.

bio|12-12|1921|Ενριέττα Σ. Λίβιτ|Henrietta Leavitt|Henrietta Leavitt was an American astronomer. She discovered the relation between the period and the luminosity of Cepheid stars, which helped to measure distances in the universe. She died in 1921.
bio|12-12|1928|Τζινγκίζ Αϊτμάτωφ|Chingiz Aitmatov|Chingiz Aitmatov was a Soviet writer from Kyrgyzstan. He wrote "Jamilya" and "The White Steamship". He died in 2008.
bio|12-12|1963|Τέοντορ Χόις|Theodor Heuss|Theodor Heuss was a German politician. He was the first president of the Federal Republic of Germany, from 1949 to 1959. He died in 1963.
bio|12-12|1970|Τζένιφερ Κόνελι|Jennifer Connelly|Jennifer Connelly is an American actress. She won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "A Beautiful Mind" and appeared in "Requiem for a Dream".
bio|12-12|1985|Αν Μπάξτερ|Ann Baxter|Ann Baxter was an American actress. She won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "The Razor's Edge" and appeared in "All About Eve". She died in 1985.

bio|12-12|1204|Μαϊμωνίδης|Maimonides|Maimonides, or Moses Maimonides, was a Jewish philosopher and physician, born in Córdoba. He wrote the "Guide for the Perplexed" and was physician to the sultan in Egypt. He died in 1204.

bio|12-13|1466|Ντονατέλλο|Donatello|Donatello was an Italian sculptor of the Renaissance from Florence. He created the bronze "David", the first free-standing nude statue since antiquity. He died in 1466.

bio|12-13|1553|Ερρίκος Δ΄|Henry IV of France|Henry IV was king of France from 1589, the first of the Bourbon dynasty. He was a Protestant and became a Catholic. With the Edict of Nantes in 1598 he granted religious tolerance. He was assassinated in 1610.
bio|12-13|1784|Σάμιουελ Τζόνσον|Samuel Johnson|Samuel Johnson died in 1784. He was an English writer and lexicographer, and he compiled the "Dictionary of the English Language".

bio|12-13|1797|Χάινριχ Χάινε|Heinrich Heine|Heinrich Heine was a German-Jewish poet. He wrote the collection "Book of Songs" and lived in Paris. Many of his poems were set to music by Schubert and Schumann. He died in 1856.

bio|12-13|1929|Κρίστοφερ Πλάμερ|Christopher Plummer|Christopher Plummer was a Canadian actor. He appeared in "The Sound of Music" and won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for "Beginners". He died in 2021.

bio|12-13|1944|Βασίλι Καντίνσκι|Wassily Kandinsky|Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian painter and art theorist. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of abstract painting. He taught at the Bauhaus and died in 1944 in France.
bio|12-13|1967|Τζέιμι Φοξ|Jamie Foxx|Jamie Foxx is an American actor and musician. He won an Oscar for his performance in "Ray", about Ray Charles.

bio|12-13|1989|Τέιλορ Σουίφτ|Taylor Swift|Taylor Swift is an American singer and songwriter. She began with country music and became one of the biggest pop stars, with albums such as "1989" and "Folklore".

bio|12-14|1503|Νοστράδαμος|Nostradamus|Nostradamus, whose real name was Michel de Nostredame, was a French doctor and astrologer. He became known for the book "Les Prophéties", with prophecies in quatrains. He died in 1566.

bio|12-14|1546|Τύχο Μπράχε|Tycho Brahe|Tycho Brahe was a Danish astronomer. He made extremely accurate observations of the stars and planets, which Johannes Kepler's assistant used for Kepler's laws. He died in 1601.

bio|12-14|1799|Τζορτζ Ουάσινγκτον|George Washington|George Washington was the 1st president of the United States, from 1789 to 1797, and commander-in-chief of the army in the War of Independence. He died in 1799.

bio|12-14|1895|Γεώργιος ΣΤ΄|George VI|George VI was king of the United Kingdom from 1936 to 1952, after the abdication of his brother Edward VIII. He led the country during the Second World War and was the father of Elizabeth II.
bio|12-14|1947|Ντίλμα Ρούσεφ|Dilma Rousseff|Dilma Rousseff is a Brazilian politician. She was the first woman president of Brazil, from 2011 to 2016, when she was removed by Congress.
bio|12-14|1988|Βανέσα Χάντζενς|Vanessa Hudgens|Vanessa Hudgens is an American actress and singer. She became known for the film "High School Musical" and also appeared in "Spring Breakers".

bio|12-14|1989|Αντρέι Ζαχάρωφ|Andrei Sakharov|Andrei Sakharov was a Soviet physicist. He contributed to the Soviet hydrogen bomb and then became an activist for human rights. In 1975 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1989.
bio|12-14|1990|Φρήντριχ Ντύρενματ|Friedrich Dürrenmatt|Friedrich Dürrenmatt was a Swiss writer and playwright. He wrote the plays "The Visit" and "The Physicists". He died in 1990.
bio|12-14|2013|Πήτερ Ο' Τουλ|Peter O'Toole|Peter O'Toole was an Irish actor, known for his role in "Lawrence of Arabia". He died in 2013 and had been nominated for an Oscar eight times.

bio|12-15|37|Νέρων|Nero|Nero was born in 37 AD and was Roman emperor from 54 to 68, the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty. His reign is known for tyranny and for the Great Fire of Rome in 64. He took his own life in 68.

bio|12-15|1675|Γιοχάνες Βερμέερ|Johannes Vermeer|Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter of the Golden Age. He painted "Girl with a Pearl Earring" and scenes of everyday life, with particular care for light. His burial date is 15 December 1675.

bio|12-15|1832|Γκυστάβ Άιφελ|Gustave Eiffel|Gustave Eiffel was a French engineer. He designed the Eiffel Tower for the Paris World's Fair of 1889 and the framework of the Statue of Liberty. He died in 1923.

bio|12-15|1852|Ανρί Μπεκερέλ|Henri Becquerel|Henri Becquerel was a French physicist. He discovered radioactivity in 1896, and in 1903 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre and Marie Curie. He died in 1908.

bio|12-15|1857|Ουίλιαμ Χάουαρντ Ταφτ|William Howard Taft|William Howard Taft was the 27th president of the United States, from 1909 to 1913, and later chief justice of the Supreme Court. He died in 1930.
bio|12-15|1859|Λουδοβίκος Λάζαρος Ζαμένχοφ|Ludwik Zamenhof|Ludwik Zamenhof was a Polish doctor and linguist. He created the international auxiliary language Esperanto in 1887. He died in 1917.

bio|12-15|1890|Καθιστός Ταύρος|Sitting Bull|Sitting Bull, also known as Tatanka Iyotake, was a chief and spiritual leader of the Lakota Sioux. He led the resistance against the United States and took part in the Battle of the Little Bighorn. He was killed in 1890 by Indian police.

bio|12-15|1958|Βόλφγκανγκ Πάουλι|Wolfgang Pauli|Wolfgang Pauli was an Austrian physicist. He formulated the Pauli exclusion principle and predicted the existence of the neutrino. In 1945 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1958.
bio|12-15|1966|Ουώλτ Ντίσνεϋ|Walt Disney|Walt Disney died in 1966. He was an American animator and producer. He created Mickey Mouse and founded the Disney studios and Disneyland.
bio|12-16|705|Γου Ζετιάν|Wu Zetian|Wu Zetian was the only woman to rule China as empress, from 690 to 705, founding her own dynasty. She died in 705.

bio|12-16|1770|Λούντβιχ βαν Μπετόβεν|Ludwig van Beethoven|Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer, one of the greatest in history. He wrote nine symphonies and many concertos and continued to compose despite his deafness. He was born in Bonn and died in 1827. 16 December is the traditional date of his birth.
bio|12-16|1775|Τζέιν Όστεν|Jane Austen|Jane Austen was an English writer. She wrote the novels "Pride and Prejudice" and "Emma". She died in 1817.
bio|12-16|1866|Βασίλι Καντίνσκι|Wassily Kandinsky|Wassily Kandinsky was born in 1866 in Moscow. He was a painter and a pioneer of abstract art. He died in 1944.
bio|12-16|1897|Αλφόνς Ντωντέ|Alphonse Daudet|Alphonse Daudet was a French writer. He wrote "Letters from My Windmill" and "Tartarin of Tarascon". He died in 1897.

bio|12-16|1917|Άρθουρ Κλαρκ|Arthur C. Clarke|Arthur C. Clarke was an English science fiction writer. He wrote "2001: A Space Odyssey" and proposed the use of communications satellites in geostationary orbit. He died in 2008.
bio|12-16|1921|Καμίγ Σαιν-Σανς|Camille Saint-Saëns|Camille Saint-Saëns was a French composer. He wrote "The Carnival of the Animals" and the Organ Symphony. He died in 1921.

bio|12-16|1928|Φίλιπ Κ. Ντικ|Philip K. Dick|Philip K. Dick was an American science fiction writer. He wrote "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?", which inspired the film "Blade Runner". He died in 1982.
bio|12-16|1965|Ουίλιαμ Σόμερσετ Μομ|W. Somerset Maugham|W. Somerset Maugham was an English writer. He wrote the novels "Of Human Bondage" and "The Painted Veil". He died in 1965.

bio|12-17|1273|Τζελαλεντίν Ρουμί|Jalal al-Din Rumi|Jalal al-Din Rumi was a Persian poet and mystic of Islam. He wrote the "Masnavi" and founded the order of the whirling dervishes. He died in 1273 in Konya.
bio|12-17|1778|Χάμφρι Ντέιβι|Humphry Davy|Humphry Davy was an English chemist. He discovered the elements sodium and potassium by electrolysis and invented the miners' safety lamp. He died in 1829.
bio|12-17|1797|Τζόζεφ Χένρι|Joseph Henry|Joseph Henry was an American physicist. He discovered self-inductance and was the first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution. He died in 1878.

bio|12-17|1830|Σιμόν Μπολίβαρ|Simón Bolívar|Simón Bolívar died in 1830. He was a Venezuelan military leader and the leader of the struggle for the independence of the countries of South America from Spain, and he is called "the Liberator".

bio|12-17|1907|Ουίλιαμ Τόμσον|William Thomson, Lord Kelvin|William Thomson, Lord Kelvin, was a Scottish physicist and engineer. He contributed to thermodynamics, and the unit of temperature, the kelvin, bears his name. He died in 1907.
bio|12-17|1975|Μίλα Γιόβοβιτς|Milla Jovovich|Milla Jovovich was born in Kiev and is an American actress and model. She became known with the film "The Fifth Element" and the series "Resident Evil".
bio|12-17|1978|Μάνι Πακιάο|Manny Pacquiao|Manny Pacquiao is a former Filipino boxer and politician. He won titles in eight weight divisions and was a senator in the Philippines.
bio|12-17|2011|Κιμ Γιονγκ Ιλ|Kim Jong-il|Kim Jong-il was the leader of North Korea from 1994 until his death in 2011. He was the son of Kim Il-sung and was succeeded by his son Kim Jong-un.

bio|12-18|1803|Γιόχαν Γκότφριντ Χέρντερ|Johann Gottfried Herder|Johann Gottfried Herder was a German philosopher and theologian. He studied language and history and influenced Romanticism. He died in 1803.

bio|12-18|1829|Ζαν Μπατίστ Λαμάρκ|Jean-Baptiste Lamarck|Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French biologist. He formulated one of the first theories of the evolution of species and introduced the term "biology". He died in 1829.
bio|12-18|1856|Τζ. Τζ. Τόμσον|J. J. Thomson|J. J. Thomson was an English physicist. He discovered the electron in 1897 and in 1906 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1940.

bio|12-18|1878|Ιωσήφ Στάλιν|Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin, whose real name was Ioseb Jughashvili, was the Soviet leader from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953. He ruled as a dictator, and millions of people were executed or imprisoned during his time. His birth date is given differently in the sources.
bio|12-18|1946|Στίβεν Σπίλμπεργκ|Steven Spielberg|Steven Spielberg is an American director and producer. He directed "Jaws", "E.T.", "Indiana Jones" and "Schindler's List", for which he won an Oscar.

bio|12-18|1963|Μπραντ Πιτ|Brad Pitt|Brad Pitt is an American actor and producer. He appeared in "Fight Club", "Se7en" and "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood", for which he won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor.
bio|12-18|1980|Κριστίνα Αγκιλέρα|Christina Aguilera|Christina Aguilera is an American singer and actress. She became known with hits such as "Genie in a Bottle" and "Beautiful".

bio|12-18|1995|Κόνραντ Τσούζε|Konrad Zuse|Konrad Zuse was a German engineer. He built the Z3 in 1941, the first programmable and fully working computer, and he is regarded as one of the pioneers of computer science. He died in 1995.
bio|12-18|2011|Βάτσλαβ Χάβελ|Václav Havel|Václav Havel died in 2011. He was a Czech playwright and dissident, and he became president of Czechoslovakia in 1989, after the Velvet Revolution.

bio|12-19|1111|Αλ-Γκαζαλί|Al-Ghazali|Al-Ghazali was a Persian philosopher and theologian of Islam. He wrote "The Incoherence of the Philosophers" and was an important figure of Sunni Islam. He died in 1111.
bio|12-19|1848|Έμιλι Μπροντέ|Emily Brontë|Emily Brontë died in 1848. She was an English writer and wrote the novel "Wuthering Heights".

bio|12-19|1852|Άλμπερτ Αβραάμ Μάικελσον|Albert Abraham Michelson|Albert Abraham Michelson was born in what is now Poland and became an American physicist. With Morley he carried out the Michelson-Morley experiment, and in 1907 he became the first American to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1931.

bio|12-19|1906|Λεονίντ Μπρέζνιεφ|Leonid Brezhnev|Leonid Brezhnev was the leader of the Soviet Union from 1964 until his death in 1982. His period is called "stagnation" and it led to the invasion of Afghanistan.
bio|12-19|1915|Εντίθ Πιάφ|Édith Piaf|Édith Piaf was a French singer, known as "the little sparrow". She sang hits such as "La vie en rose" and "Non, je ne regrette rien". She died in 1963.
bio|12-19|1934|Πρατίμπχα Πατίλ|Pratibha Patil|Pratibha Patil is an Indian politician. She was the first woman president of India, from 2007 to 2012.

bio|12-19|1953|Ρόμπερτ Άντριους Μίλικαν|Robert Andrews Millikan|Robert Andrews Millikan was an American physicist. He measured the charge of the electron with the oil-drop experiment and in 1923 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1953.
bio|12-19|1987|Καρίμ Μπενζεμά|Karim Benzema|Karim Benzema is a French footballer, a striker. He played for Lyon and Real Madrid and won the Ballon d'Or in 2022.
bio|12-19|1996|Μαρτσέλλο Μαστρογιάννι|Marcello Mastroianni|Marcello Mastroianni died in 1996. He was an Italian actor who became known for Fellini's "La Dolce Vita" and "8½".

bio|12-20|1890|Γιάροσλαβ Χέιροφσκι|Jaroslav Heyrovský|Jaroslav Heyrovský was a Czech chemist. He discovered polarography, a method of analysis, and in 1959 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1967.

bio|12-20|1927|Κιμ Γιόνγκ-σαμ|Kim Young-sam|Kim Young-sam was a South Korean politician. He was president of South Korea from 1993 to 1998, the first civilian president after decades of military rule. He died in 2015.

bio|12-20|1937|Έριχ Λούντεντορφ|Erich Ludendorff|Erich Ludendorff was a German general. He was the chief of staff of the German army in the First World War and took part in the Beer Hall Putsch of 1923. He died in 1937.
bio|12-20|1955|Μπιναλί Γιλντιρίμ|Binali Yıldırım|Binali Yıldırım is a Turkish politician. He was the last prime minister of Turkey, from 2016 to 2018, before the office was abolished.

bio|12-20|1956|Μοχάμεντ Ουλντ Αμπντέλ Αζίζ|Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz|Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz is a Mauritanian military officer and politician. He took power in a coup in 2008 and was president of Mauritania until 2019.

bio|12-20|1968|Τζον Στάινμπεκ|John Steinbeck|John Steinbeck was an American writer. He wrote the novels "The Grapes of Wrath" and "Of Mice and Men". In 1962 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1968.
bio|12-20|1996|Καρλ Σαγκάν|Carl Sagan|Carl Sagan died in 1996. He was an American astronomer and popular writer, known for the book and television series "Cosmos".

bio|12-20|1998|Κιλιάν Εμπαπέ|Kylian Mbappé|Kylian Mbappé is a French footballer, a striker. He played for Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, won the World Cup in 2018 and scored a hat-trick in the final of 2022.
bio|12-20|2001|Λεοπόλντ Σεντάρ Σανγκόρ|Léopold Sédar Senghor|Léopold Sédar Senghor was a Senegalese poet and the first president of Senegal, from 1960 to 1980. He died in 2001.
bio|12-21|1375|Βοκάκιος|Boccaccio|Giovanni Boccaccio was an Italian writer and humanist. He wrote the "Decameron", a collection of one hundred stories. He died in 1375.

bio|12-21|1804|Μπέντζαμιν Ντισραέλι|Benjamin Disraeli|Benjamin Disraeli was a British Conservative politician and writer. He was prime minister of the United Kingdom in 1868 and from 1874 to 1880. He died in 1881.
bio|12-21|1937|Τζέιν Φόντα|Jane Fonda|Jane Fonda is an American actress and activist. She won two Oscars, for "Klute" and "Coming Home".
bio|12-21|1940|Φράνσις Σκοτ Φιτζέραλντ|F. Scott Fitzgerald|F. Scott Fitzgerald died in 1940. He was an American writer who wrote "The Great Gatsby".
bio|12-21|1942|Χου Ζιντάο|Hu Jintao|Hu Jintao is a Chinese politician. He was president of China and general secretary of the Communist Party from 2002 to 2012.

bio|12-21|1945|Τζωρτζ Σμιθ Πάττον|George S. Patton|George S. Patton was an American general. He commanded the Third Army in Western Europe during the Second World War and had a controversial personality. He died in 1945 from injuries received in a road accident.
bio|12-21|1967|Μιχαήλ Σαακασβίλι|Mikheil Saakashvili|Mikheil Saakashvili is a Georgian politician. He led the "Rose Revolution" in 2003 and was president of Georgia from 2004 to 2013.
bio|12-21|1977|Εμμανουέλ Μακρόν|Emmanuel Macron|Emmanuel Macron is a French politician. He became president of France in 2017, at the age of 39, and was re-elected in 2022.

bio|12-21|2006|Σαπαρμουράτ Νιγιαζόφ|Saparmurat Niyazov|Saparmurat Niyazov was the first president of Turkmenistan, from 1991 to 2006. He governed in an authoritarian way and created a cult of personality.
bio|12-22|69|Βιτέλλιος|Vitellius|Vitellius was a Roman emperor in 69, in the "Year of the Four Emperors". He was killed on 22 December 69 by the followers of Vespasian.

bio|12-22|244|Διοκλητιανός|Diocletian|Diocletian was Roman emperor from 284 to 305. He established the Tetrarchy and ordered the last great persecution of Christians. The exact year and date of his birth are uncertain.
bio|12-22|1639|Ρακίνας|Jean Racine|Jean Racine was a French playwright. He wrote the tragedies "Phaedra", "Andromache" and "Britannicus", inspired by ancient Greek mythology. He died in 1699.
bio|12-22|1858|Τζάκομο Πουτσίνι|Giacomo Puccini|Giacomo Puccini was an Italian composer. He wrote the operas "La Bohème", "Tosca", "Madama Butterfly" and "Turandot". He died in 1924.
bio|12-22|1880|Τζορτζ Έλιοτ|George Eliot|George Eliot, whose real name was Mary Ann Evans, was an English writer and journalist. She wrote "Middlemarch" and "The Mill on the Floss". She died in 1880.

bio|12-22|1887|Σρινιβάσα Ραμανούτζαν|Srinivasa Ramanujan|Srinivasa Ramanujan was an Indian mathematician, self-taught. He made impressive discoveries in number theory and worked with Hardy at Cambridge. He died young, in 1920, at the age of 32.
bio|12-22|1984|Basshunter|Basshunter|Basshunter, whose real name is Jonas Alder, is a Swedish singer and electronic music producer. He became known with the song "Boten Anna".

bio|12-22|1989|Σάμιουελ Μπέκετ|Samuel Beckett|Samuel Beckett was an Irish writer who lived in France. He wrote the play "Waiting for Godot" and in 1969 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1989.

bio|12-22|2014|Τζο Κόκερ|Joe Cocker|Joe Cocker was an English singer with a raspy voice. He became known for "With a Little Help from My Friends" at Woodstock and for "Up Where We Belong". He died in 2014.
bio|12-23|1777|Αλέξανδρος Α΄|Alexander I|Alexander I was tsar of Russia from 1801 to 1825. He defeated Napoleon in 1812 and was a leader of the Holy Alliance. He died in 1825.

bio|12-23|1790|Ζαν-Φρανσουά Σαμπολιόν|Jean-François Champollion|Jean-François Champollion was a French Egyptologist. He deciphered the hieroglyphs in 1822 with the help of the Rosetta Stone. He died in 1832.
bio|12-23|1805|Τζόζεφ Σμιθ|Joseph Smith|Joseph Smith was an American religious leader and the founder of the Mormon movement. He published the "Book of Mormon" in 1830. He was killed in 1844.
bio|12-23|1918|Χέλμουτ Σμιτ|Helmut Schmidt|Helmut Schmidt was a German Social Democrat politician. He was chancellor of West Germany from 1974 to 1982. He died in 2015.
bio|12-23|1933|Ακιχίτο|Akihito|Akihito was emperor of Japan from 1989 to 2019, when he abdicated, the first to do so in two centuries. He was succeeded by his son Naruhito.

bio|12-23|1948|Τότζο Χιντέκι|Hideki Tojo|Hideki Tojo was a Japanese military officer and prime minister of Japan from 1941 to 1944. He led the country into the Pacific War. He was convicted as a war criminal and hanged in 1948.
bio|12-23|1953|Λαβρέντι Μπέρια|Lavrentiy Beria|Lavrentiy Beria was a Soviet politician and head of the secret police under Stalin. After Stalin's death he was arrested and executed in 1953.
bio|12-23|1973|Γκέραρντ Κάιπερ|Gerard Kuiper|Gerard Kuiper was a Dutch-American astronomer. He discovered moons of Uranus and Neptune and predicted the Kuiper belt. He died in 1973.

bio|12-23|2013|Μιχαήλ Καλάσνικοφ|Mikhail Kalashnikov|Mikhail Kalashnikov died in 2013, at the age of 94. He was a Russian soldier and weapons designer and created the AK-47 rifle, one of the most widespread weapons in the world.
